newsitem.title: CHINA: China city to ease entry for Taiwan businessmen.
newsitem.headline: China city to ease entry for Taiwan businessmen.

text.p: Xiamen city in China's southeastern Fujian province is to ease entry and exit conditions for business people from Beijing's arch rival Taiwan, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

From September 8 Taiwanese on business or those who had bought houses in the city would be permitted to apply for two-year temporary residence certificates and multi-entry and exit visas, the official news agency said.
Their families would also enjoy the preferential terms, it said.
Xiamen lies just across the Taiwan Strait from Beijing's Nationalist-ruled island rival and is a major recipient of Taiwanese investment.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin said on Friday China's leaders were willing to travel to Taiwan, but urged the island to abandon attempts to break out of its diplomatic isolation.
Jiang said Taipei should prove it was sincere in its desire for senior-level talks by ending efforts to raise its international profile and climb out of its isolation.
China has considered Taiwan a renegade province that is not entitled to international recognition since their civil war ended in 1949.
